I. Description of the Proposal
A. General
This Environmental Statement for a Marijuana Eradication Project is being submitted in accordance with P.L. 91-190, the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969. The purpose of the Statement is to evaluate the environmental impact of the proposed action to spray 65 square acres and 65 linear miles of ditch and road shoulder with granulated form 2, 4D herbicide. The chemical formula to be used is 33 percent, 2, 4D acid ester and 67 percent clay. This is the equivalent of 20 percent 2, 4D acid or 1 lb. 2, 4D per acre which is the recommended concentration.
The formula has been approved by EPA in the past and is registered with EPA.
The ditches to be sprayed traverse Indiana Route 39. Route 39 parallels U. S. Route 35 North/South. The ditches run through Richgrove Township. Richgrove Township is a farmland community. Twenty foot strips on both sides of the ditch area for a distance of 33 miles will be sprayed. The 65 acres of land comprise or farm (90% of the acreage) and an area continguous to that farm.
B. Purpose and Need
Wild hemp (Cannabis sativa 1.) is a weed which contains powerful hallucinogenic compounds called tetrahydro-cannabinals. During World War II,
the Federal Government encouraged the cultivation of hemp for use in the
manufacture of rope to aid in the war effort. The leaves of the mature
plant can be dried and smoked, or the hallucinogenic resin can be extracted
and hardened to produce the potent hashish.
